verdict.headline: This NDA imposes perpetual, entirely one-sided secrecy obligations on you while leaving your own business submissions unprotected.
summary: The agreement defines confidential information to include public and pre-existing knowledge and enforces secrecy without exception in perpetuity.
You are required to indemnify Quillstone for legal costs on a full indemnity basis, while Quillstone gives no confidentiality undertakings for your recipes or tender data.
Only Quillstone has the right to terminate the contract, while your obligations survive indefinitely.

findings.why_risky: You are forced to treat publicly available facts and your own prior knowledge as Quillstone's confidential information. This makes compliance almost impossible and exposes your bakery to continuous liability.
findings.standard: Standard NDAs strictly exclude information that is already in the public domain, already known to the recipient, independently developed, or rightfully obtained from third parties.
findings.suggested_ask: Please narrow the definition of Confidential Information to non-public materials and add standard carve-outs for public domain and pre-existing information.

summary: This NDA imposes an aggressive 3-year regional non-compete clause that directly suppresses Lumio Tani's core agritech business.

verdict.headline: This NDA is heavily one-sided, leaving your fleet data unprotected and restricting termination.
summary: The agreement binds only you to confidentiality while explicitly giving the vendor free rein over your fleet operational data.
Only the vendor can terminate the agreement at will, locking you into five years of post-termination restrictions.
The agreement imposes a two-year post-termination non-solicitation restraint on hiring vendor employees.

verdict.headline: High-risk terms lock you into full-term fees, take away created ad materials, and withhold ad account data.
summary: The agreement binds you to pay all remaining monthly retainers if you exit early, while letting the agency retain all campaign creatives upon termination.
The agency retains sole ownership and control of your ad accounts, pixel data, and campaign history both during and after the engagement.
The 24-month non-solicitation restriction includes a 12-month fee penalty that may exceed reasonable loss under Malaysian law.

verdict.headline: This cleaning contract locks you into two-year renewals and forces you to indemnify the vendor even for their own negligence.
summary: The agreement automatically renews for two years at a time unless you give 90 days' notice by registered post.
Clause 5.1 requires you to indemnify the vendor for losses even when caused by the vendor's own negligence, while the vendor disclaims all property damage under clause 5.2.
The vendor can terminate for convenience on 7 days' notice under clause 7.2, whereas you may terminate only for uncured material breach under clause 7.1.

findings.suggested_ask: Please change renewal to 12-month periods with 30 days' notice to stop renewal by email, and require the vendor to send a reminder 60 days before the expiry date.

verdict.headline: High-risk shop lot tenancy with structural repair duties, unilateral rent hikes, non-refundable deposit terms, and lock-out clauses.
summary: The agreement makes the tenant pay for all structural repairs to the building and permits the landlord to increase rent by any amount on 14 days' notice.
The security deposit is made non-refundable at the landlord's sole discretion, and early exit requires paying all remaining rent for the term.
The landlord claims self-help rights to re-enter, change locks, and detain goods after 7 days of unpaid rent without notice or court order.

findings.title: Deposit non-refundable at landlord's discretion
findings.quote: The Security Deposit shall be non-refundable at the Landlord's discretion on the expiry or earlier termination of this Agreement, and the Landlord is not required to give reasons or to account for its decision.
findings.why_risky: The landlord can arbitrarily withhold your RM20,400 deposit without explanation. Under clause 4.2, the landlord has complete discretion to retain the full three months' rent deposit even if you have paid all sums and kept the premises in perfect condition.
findings.standard: Security deposits should be fully refundable within 14 to 30 days after handover, subject only to itemised deductions for unpaid rent or damage exceeding fair wear and tear.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the security deposit refundable within 21 days of handover back, with deductions limited to unpaid rent and utilities and damage beyond fair wear and tear, each shown by a written list or receipts.

findings.title: Uncapped rent increases on short notice
findings.quote: The Landlord may, in its sole discretion, increase the Rent by any amount and at any time, by giving the Tenant fourteen (14) days' notice, and the Tenant shall pay the new Rent from the date stated in the notice.
findings.why_risky: The landlord can unilaterally hike rent to any figure with only 14 days' notice. Under clause 5.1 and clause 5.2, you cannot challenge the revised amount or terminate the agreement in response.
findings.standard: Commercial rents should remain fixed for the term, or adjust according to an agreed cap (such as 10% to 15%) or open-market valuation with at least 2 to 3 months' notice and an exit option.
findings.suggested_ask: Please replace the landlord's discretion with a fixed schedule or a review to open-market rent capped at 10% a review, with 3 months' written notice and the tenant's right to leave if it does not accept the new rent.

findings.why_risky: You are forced to pay for structural defects to the entire building regardless of fault. Clause 6.1 imposes open-ended capital liabilities for roofs, external walls, foundations, columns, and main drainage on a ground-floor tenant.

findings.suggested_ask: Please limit the tenant's repair duty to day-to-day upkeep and damage the tenant causes; the landlord keeps the structure and the main services, with repairs done within 14 days of notice.

verdict.headline: High risk due to full deposit forfeiture on early exit, automatic two-year renewals, and unequal termination notice.
summary: The agreement forfeits your entire deposit if you vacate early, regardless of actual loss.
It locks you into automatic two-year renewals unless you give 60 days' written notice.
The landlord can evict you on 7 days' notice for any reason, whereas you must provide 2 months' notice.

findings.why_risky: You lose your entire RM1,500 deposit if you leave early, even if you give advance notice or the landlord suffers no loss. Under clause 4.3, this applies regardless of actual losses or how quickly the landlord finds a replacement.
findings.standard: The deposit should be returned minus actual unpaid rent, utility bills, or reasonable re-letting costs while the landlord seeks a replacement tenant.
findings.suggested_ask: Please amend clause 4.3 so that early termination requires one month's notice or fee, with the remaining deposit returned after deducting actual unpaid rent and utilities.
